title: EU / UK Jurisdictional Exchange Playbook (onramp + ops simulations)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact playbook for onboarding enterprise customers who require strict data locality between the EU and the UK. It focuses on the operational exchange model (how customer data and audit evidence are exchanged across EU/UK boundaries), the escrow test patterns we run during onboarding, and the simulated failure scenarios operators should exercise before handoff. The goal is practical runbooks and sample answers for Sales/SE + Legal to use in contract negotiation and for SRE/Platform to run validation pre-production.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: cross-border exchange behavior for hosted and private deployments where customer contract requires data to remain in one legal territory but allows certain escrow/forensics exchange under documented procedures (e.g., EU primary with UK-accessible audit evidence).
- Audience: Platform engineers, SRE oncall, Solutions Engineering (pre-sales), Customer Security/Legal reviewers, Professional Services onboarding team.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Customer selects primary jurisdiction (EU or UK) in onboarding form.
- Primary inference workload (tokens, KV cache) is kept in primary jurisdiction compute/storage.
- Audit evidence (logs, sanitized traces, proof packages) may be packaged and transferred to a secured escrow bucket in the other jurisdiction when contractually permitted.
- All transfers are encrypted in transit (TLS1.3) and at rest (KMS-wrapped).
- KMS and key policies reflect jurisdictional requirements; cross-region key wrapping is reviewed for legal acceptance.

Key concepts and definitions (brief):
- Primary Domain: where live inference compute and customer data are processed and stored.
- Escrow Bundle: time-bounded package of audit artifacts (manifest, hashes, sanitized logs, retention labels) prepared for cross-border transfer under contract.
- Exchange Window: pre-negotiated schedule or triggered event when an Escrow Bundle is allowed to leave the Primary Domain for the counter-jurisdiction.

Operator checklist: pre-onboarding (SRE / PS)
1) Verify tenancy metadata: confirm customer account shows jurisdiction: EU or UK, legal contact, allowed-exchange flag (yes/no), and Exchange Window policy id.
2) Provision primary compute in appropriate region sets (example: eu-west-1 family for EU, eu-uk-1 for UK) and assert node affinity labels.
3) Review KMS config: ensure key policies do not allow automatic cross-region decryption except for escrow key-wrapping tasks tied to a service principal.
4) Escrow storage: create escrow bucket in counter-jurisdiction with restricted access role and short-lived tokens. Document the bucket ARN/ID in customer onboarding file.
5) Test-run: perform a dry-run escrow creation locally and validate the bundle manifest signs with expected signing key (JWS) and that integrity checks pass.
6) Telemetry: register customer in residency telemetry sheet and configure synthetic traces for Exchange Window runs.

Escrow Bundle contents and format (minimum):
- manifest.json (metadata: customer_id, primary_domain, exchange_window, artifacts list, generation_timestamp)
- artifacts/trace-sanitized.json.gz (redacted PII, hashed tokens for traceability)
- artifacts/kv-usage-summary.csv (per-request token counts by route)
- signature.jws (signed by Redwood-residency-signing key)
- retention.txt (TTL and permitted recipients)
Note: bundles should avoid including PII or raw user prompts unless contract explicitly permits. If raw content is included, ensure an explicit data subject consent and legal ticket.

Onboarding QA: sample questions & short answers for Sales/Legal
Q: "Can you guarantee a full copy of logs will never leave the EU?"
A: "We guarantee primary compute and primary storage remain in the EU. Logs required for operational debugging remain in the EU by default. Escrow transfers are only performed if the contract sets an Exchange Window and explicit permitted purpose; such transfers are recorded, signed, and minimally scoped."

Q: "What measures ensure an escrow bundle is authentic and untampered?"
A: "All bundles are signed (JWS) with our residency signing key. Receipts (hashes) are recorded both in our audit ledger and in a per-customer evidence record. The operator must validate signature and manifest before ingestion in the counter-jurisdiction."

Simulated failure scenarios to exercise (run weekly during onboarding):
- Scenario A: Incomplete Escrow Bundle generation (missing signature). Expected response: operator-run abort, alert to SRE channel, create incident JIRA with tag JIRA-OP-8765 and rerun.
- Scenario B: Escrow upload ACL mismatch (unexpected public-read flag). Expected response: automated detection via preflight ACL scanner, revoke object, rotate temp credentials, notify legal team.
- Scenario C: Cross-region key unwrap denied by KMS policy. Response: escalate to infra security, do not transfer bundle, record incident and hold Exchange Window.
- Scenario D: Consumer requests immediate forensic export outside scheduled Exchange Window. Response: require legal ticket + signed request; deny by default and route to Customer Security for approval.

Operational play for Exchange Window run (operators):
Step 0: Confirm Exchange Window active or signed approval exists.
Step 1: Trigger bundle generator on primary domain (CLI: residency-bundle create --customer <id> --window <id>).
Step 2: Run local preflight validator (residency-bundle validate --in <file>), assert signature and manifest completeness.
Step 3: KMS wrap the bundle key and stage to temporary escrow bucket in counter-jurisdiction via transfer-agent with restricted role.
Step 4: Generate evidence receipt: ledger entry with timestamp, bundle-hash, operator-id. Publish receipt to customer ledger and legal-repository.
Step 5: Notify Solutions Engineering and Customer Security that transfer completed; attach evidence and retention controls.
Step 6: Schedule post-transfer verification job (24h) to re-validate bucket ACLs and access logs.

Minimal automation checks (SRE should add to rollout checklist):
- preflight: manifest schema validation, signature present, artifacts count matches manifest, hash matches.
- ACL-scan: ensure bucket ACLs and object-level ACLs set to expected role set.
- KMS policy check: ensure unwrap call only from transfer-agent principal.
- Telemetry: synthetic trace emitted with tag residency.bundle.<customer_id> for monitoring.

Evidence packaging for audits:
- Provide the customer with the evidence receipt and manifest. For Redwood internal audits, archive a copy of the signed bundle in secure long-term evidence store (retention per contract). Keep chain-of-custody log for 7 years or per regulatory requirement.

Customer communication templates (sample):
- Template subject: "Planned Exchange Window: evidence package for <customer>"
- Body excerpt (short): "We will generate and transfer an Escrow Bundle (manifest + sanitized artifacts) on <date> as per Section X of your residency agreement. The bundle will be signed and available at <bucket> for the next 30 days. Contact security@redwood with any questions."

Open questions & action items (owners tagged):
- Confirm whether raw full-chat transcripts are permissible in escrow bundles for regulated financial customers (Owner: Legal - Sophie Navarro; ticket: LEG-1321).
- Add automated ACL remediation play to transfer-agent (Owner: Infra - Marcus Lee; JIRA: INFRA-4222).
- Define retention TTL policy per EU-UK product SKU (Owner: Product - Aisha Patel; product-ticket: PROD-2190).

Appendix: quick operator commands and expected logs (examples)
- residency-bundle create --customer X --window W  => logs: "bundle-gen start", "bundle-gen complete", "signature-ok"
- residency-bundle validate --file bndl.tgz => returns "manifest-ok, artifacts=4, signature=valid"
- transfer-agent push --to escrow://bucket-y  => logs: "upload-start", "upload-complete", "acl-set:"role/escrow-agent""

Notes and constraints: keep the exchange playbook conservative. If in doubt about including raw user content in the exchange bundle, err on the side of exclusion and escalate to Legal. This document is intentionally operational and not legal advice. For finalized contract language, coordinate with Legal (Sophie Navarro).

Next steps before final handoff:
- Run three live dry-runs for the first two enterprise customers scheduled this quarter and collect telemetry.
- Bake the preflight validator into CI so every release that touches residency-bundle generation runs the manifest tests.
- Move this doc to Confluence page RESIDENCY-EXCHANGE-PLAYBOOK and reference from onboarding checklist.

Revision history: 2025-10-12 initial draft by Aisha Patel; 2025-11-08 added failure scenarios (Marcus L.); 2026-03-10 edited for Exchange Window automation notes (Ibrahim K.).
